what_it_does: Tensor cores are dedicated hardware units inside a GPU designed to perform large matrix multiplications (multiplying two grids of numbers together) very quickly — a fundamental operation in AI training and inference. Vortex is an open-source research GPU built around the RISC-V instruction set (a freely available chip instruction vocabulary). This paper adds tensor core hardware to Vortex and then studies why it is often underused: the bottleneck turns out to be memory bandwidth (data cannot be fed to the cores fast enough) and contention between the many simultaneous thread groups (called warps) competing to use the same core. The fix is cooperative warp execution — multiple warps team up to share a single tensor core invocation, reducing each warp's individual data requirements and letting memory fetches and computation overlap better. This is from the abstract only.
